title: Neurons, axonal transport and nerve repair
source_evidence: Full L54–55 publisher captions and 32 assigned topics through closing activities; inherited bounded visual audit of 8 sheets, 137 sampled stills, 24 selected native frames; no continuous video/audio.

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach neuron and chemical/electrical synapse with explicit pre/post compartments. Caption's “nerve is a coiled group of whole neurons” is wrong; a PNS nerve is axon bundles with glial, connective and vascular components.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach dendrite, soma, axon initial segment, myelin/node and presynaptic terminal. A single multipolar diagram is representative, not all neurons; hillock versus trigger segment must be distinguished.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach dendritic ligand-gated channels and metabotropic GPCRs; “G-coupled” caption terminology is imprecise and not every dendrite is a passive antenna. Receptor binding is not universal uptake.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach soma nucleus/ribosomes/ER/Golgi roles. Local axonal translation exists for some products, so “all protein synthesis in soma” would overstate the diagram.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach DNA **transcription** → mRNA → ribosomal translation → protein sorting, with L54 native `f0022` as slide evidence. Caption 10:40/11:25 inserts replication as required, incorrectly; DNA replication is not required for routine neuronal protein synthesis. Nucleus does not itself translate protein. Some transmitters are small molecules, not proteins.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach myelin internodes and exposed nodes for membrane conduction; do not depict actual action potential teleportation or mix it with molecular cargo. Specify Schwann (PNS) versus oligodendrocyte (CNS) myelin.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach microtubule-polarity-based kinesin anterograde and dynein retrograde **as the cited exemplars**, with cargo-specific adapters. Native `f0029` confirms direction; not all axonal material is a transmitter vesicle, and local recycling occurs.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach retrograde injury signaling and anterograde delivery of new material as distinct traffic. Native `f0036/f0039` annotate both. Caption 17:53 assigns outward healing cargo to dynein, contradicting its own earlier definition; correct to outward kinesin-family transport in this teaching schematic. Growth factors can signal via endosomes; avoid an all-purpose literal healing-protein narrative.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach viral exploitation of axonal transport only with **virus-, receptor-, cell- and direction-specific** caveats. Native `f0033` groups polio/rabies/herpes as one mechanism; captions claim all fuse with nucleus/change genes. Rabies and poliovirus are RNA viruses with distinct replication biology; do not universalize nuclear fusion or clinical course.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach saltatory conduction as local internodal current and nodal regeneration; native `f0043` gives up-to-120 vs 0.5–10 m/s as broad class figures. Speed depends on diameter, temperature, myelin and fiber class; neither number is an invariant. A millisecond voltage event is not the same clock as cargo transport or days-long repair.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach presynaptic AP → voltage-gated Ca²⁺ entry → primed SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion and synaptotagmin Ca²⁺ sensing, then transmitter binding to postsynaptic receptors. Native `f0047` correctly labels the axon terminal presynaptic; caption 23:49 calls it postsynaptic, and 22:57 says Ca²⁺ binds SNARE as the trigger. Clearance is transmitter-dependent (transporters, enzymatic breakdown, diffusion/glia), not universal dynein return to soma/lysosomal amino acids.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach multipolar, bipolar and **pseudounipolar** morphologies; native `f0055` multipolar and contact-sheet bipolar/unipolar cartoon. Human primary somatosensory ganglion neurons are pseudounipolar, not a simple one-process unipolar class. Retina contains bipolar interneurons, with location/function specified.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach afferent, efferent and interneuron as pathway roles, not rigid shape categories. Native `f0059` says “unipolar” sensory; qualify human pseudounipolar and distinguish somatic/autonomic motor fibers.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach endoneurium around individual **axons**, perineurium around fascicles, epineurium around the nerve. Native `f0065` gives a mostly correct written hierarchy but calls the extracted object “neurone”; no soma is normally in each axonal fascicle cross section.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach why endoneurial tubes/fascicular organization constrain repair. Caption's “doctor fuses perineuria” is overliteral and not a general operation/recovery guarantee. **Late L54 activity visibly confirmed** `f0069` at 34:00: “which neuron sends signal faster?” Reframe as a comparison with specified axon diameter, myelination, path length and synapse count. Native `f0068` claims hundreds of miles could circle Earth >2 times, an internal arithmetic impossibility; exclude.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach mixed spinal nerve from dorsal sensory and ventral motor roots, then axon/Schwann/endoneurium/fascicle/perineurium/epineurium. Dorsal-root ganglion is not inside each peripheral nerve fascicle.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach cut, crush, stretch, compression, metabolic/infectious and iatrogenic causes as etiologically different; mechanism and grade cannot be inferred from cause word alone. No symptom-only diagnosis.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach Seddon's neurapraxia, axonotmesis, neurotmesis as a **coarse** three-class scheme, with Sunderland grades and mixed lesions as needed. Native `f0016` class slide correctly identifies axonal discontinuity for axonotmesis; caption 07:26 wrongly says myelin-only.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach neurapraxia as focal conduction block with axonal continuity, sometimes focal myelin disturbance. Native `f0020` labels intact axon. **No distal Wallerian axon degeneration** in this class; improvement varies and cannot be inferred from the single sleeping-arm anecdote.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach axonotmesis as axonal interruption with some connective guidance preserved; distal Wallerian degeneration follows. Source's “endoneurium always intact” is too narrow across Sunderland subgrades. Recovery depends on distance, alignment, target survival and lesion severity, not guaranteed in 5 days–6 months.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach neurotmesis as complete nerve disruption in the canonical class. Native `f0024/f0029` show broken axon and sheaths; don't conclude universal complete paralysis or zero natural potential from one cartoon. Repair/graft decisions are clinical, not an automatic instruction.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach Wallerian degeneration in axonotmesis/neurotmesis after axonal disconnection. Native `f0033` says so; caption 14:02 includes neurapraxia but narrows to axonotmesis at 14:57. This is the major SCI-020 correction.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach chromatolysis as somatic injury response with swelling, nuclear eccentricity and **Nissl substance dispersal**, not nuclear pile-up of Nissl/Golgi. Native `f0033/f0037` says dispersion; caption 15:38–16:18 says concentration near nucleus. Do not make it a mandatory first temporal step before every distal event.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach surviving soma-connected proximal stump vs disconnected distal axon; native `f0042` marks both. Proximal local retraction can occur, while distal Wallerian breakdown defines the disconnection response.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach distal axon/myelin fragmentation and clearance over time; a distal empty guide tube is a simplified end state, not surviving distal axon resurrecting. Native `f0049` redraws endpoint but does not show in-vivo timing.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach Schwann repair-state transition and macrophage recruitment/clearance. Native `f0042` states endoneurium “produces serotonin and histamine” as the causal mechanism; omit absent direct tissue-specific evidence. Schwann cells do not simply almost all die; their survival/reprogramming is central to repair.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach axon regeneration from a **surviving proximal neuron** into permissive distal paths, with remyelination and target reconnection separate outcomes. No automatic complete functional recovery.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach growth cones/sprouts from the proximal stump; native `f0053` draws a single successful bridge, an idealized pathway, not a measured patient trajectory.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach Schwann repair cells/Bands of Büngner as guidance and trophic support, with species/evidence scope. Native `f0056` says Schwann cells regrow to remyelinate; distinguish repair phenotype, axon regrowth, then remyelination.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Treat 1–3 mm/day as a rough **axon elongation** teaching estimate, not a promise of functional recovery or a constant for every human nerve. If used in a worked distance/time problem, state no delay/branching/mismatch assumptions and do not call the answer prognosis.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach lesion distance to soma/target and cell survival as factors; the caption's near-soma → no Schwann cells → cell-body death chain is too absolute. Keep injury site, viable cell body, distal pathway and target as independent conditions.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Teach CNS vs PNS repair environments, scar/inhibitors, inflammation and plasticity as **relative constraints**. Native `f0061` and caption say oligodendrocytes “cannot remyelinate” and CNS repair impossible; human MS lesions demonstrate some oligodendroglial remyelination. Astrocytes are CNS glia, so “few in PNS” is a poor PNS comparison. **Late L55 activity visible** `f0066` at 32:30: Wallerian class, best prognosis, often surgical class. Correct responses: axonal injury classes, typical neurapraxia, and severe neurotmesis may need repair evaluation; avoid individual prognosis. The prompt says “PNS or CNS?” although Wallerian degeneration can occur after axonal injury in both compartments, with different clearance/regrowth.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending
